chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) fell ill with three illnesses. During every illness he bequeathed with a bequest, so when he recovered, he signed (approved) his bequest.
ai.seo_question: What was the practice of Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn regarding his wills during times of illness?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the meticulous legal prudence of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (as), who repeated the drafting and validation of his will across three separate illnesses to ensure its authenticity and prevent disputes among heirs. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the formalization of bequests (wasiyya) as a crucial mechanism for distributing wealth, particularly in favor of charity and specific family members, in accordance with prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> fell ill with three illnesses. During every illness he<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed with a bequest, so when he<sup>asws</sup> came around, signed (approved) his<sup>asws</sup> bequest’.
en.sarwar: 14. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has narrated the following: “
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, became ill three times, each time he made a will and when he recovered from his illness he approved his will.’”
